title: Game Math Part 2 · Planes and Triangles 1: Distance to a Surface

scenes.title: 상자로 고른 후보에서 실제 표면으로
lines: The previous chapter built connections and target bounds. Overlapping bounds select a candidate, but do not yet tell us whether a point reaches the surface.
This chapter has two episodes. First, define the surface orientation, distance and closest point. Next, test whether the point lies within a triangle and calculate its color.

scenes.title: 바닥까지의 거리와 삼각형 안의 위치
lines: How do we calculate a point distance from a floor and its location within a triangle?
We will observe game platforms and terrain, then calculate plane normals and signed distances.
Next we will build a triangle from three points and work out its area and barycentric coordinates.
Finally we will reject an off-plane query and use the same coordinates to interpolate color.

scenes.title: 발판의 표면을 기준으로 보기
lines: Observe the top surface of a bridge in Poly Bridge 3.
Distinguish the vehicle’s height from the bridge surface. In our model, test whether a point of an object lies above the surface or approaches it.
Mathematics can simplify that reference to a plane. A real platform has thickness and edges; a plane extends infinitely.
Distance to the surface and remaining within the platform footprint are separate tests.
Camera motion changes its screen appearance. Calculations must use points and normals defined in one coordinate frame.
This footage motivates a reference surface; it does not reveal the game internal collision representation.

scenes.title: 바닥을 따라가는 화살표와 수직 화살표
lines: A direction along the floor differs from one pointing straight away from it. A plane is a flat surface extending indefinitely; its normal is perpendicular to the surface. The normal itself is not the floor height.

Set the floor height to2 and choose the upward normal(0,1,0). A dot product multiplies matching components and adds them. Here only y remains. Matching the floor height2 places the point on this plane.

scenes.title: 바닥에서 떨어졌다가 표면으로 돌아옵니다
lines: Observe a floor model and a point above it. Move the point parallel to the floor, then vertically. Moving along a surface differs from moving away from it.
Lower the point perpendicularly back to the floor. Green marks a direction along the surface; blue marks its normal direction. Distinguish these directions when calculating distance.

scenes.title: 평면의 방향과 위치를 나누기
lines: Describe a plane with a normal and a location coefficient. The normal points perpendicular to the surface.
Every point on the plane has the same dot product with its normal. Call that coefficient d.
The normal has components zero, one, zero. Constant d equals two. Every point with y equal to two lies on this plane.
The y zero plane contains the origin; the y two plane does not. A general plane is an affine set, not necessarily a linear subspace.
Subtracting two plane points gives a direction along the plane. Its dot product with the normal is zero.
Reversing the normal swaps front and back. Reverse d as well to preserve the same plane.

scenes.title: 같은 바닥인데 대입값은 왜 두 배일까요?
lines: The floor is still y equals two. A point at y five is three units away. Multiplying both sides by two gives two y equals four, which describes the same floor.

Substituting five now gives a residual of six. Neither the floor nor the point moved; the equation scale doubled. Undo that scale to obtain perpendicular distance. For a general orientation, the scale is the normal length.

scenes.title: 식의 값과 실제 거리를 구분하기
lines: Evaluate the normal dot point minus d. A positive value lies on the normal side; a negative value lies on the opposite side.
The normal has components zero, two, zero. Constant d equals four. This is still the y-equals-two plane, and the normal length is two.
At point four, five, minus three, the dot product is ten. Subtracting four gives six, but six is not the distance.
Divide by normal length two to get signed distance three. Only a unit normal makes the raw residual a distance.
Normalize both the normal and d by two. Normalizing only the normal changes the plane location.
A zero-length normal cannot define a plane direction. Validate before division.

scenes.title: 발판의 위치와 경사를 따로 봅니다
lines: This time the middle of the bridge opens.
The bridge sections tilt while their outer ends stay connected. Horizontal and tilted sections have different orientations. In our model, rotate a surface together with its perpendicular normal.
Even for the same point, changing a surface position or orientation changes its distance from that surface. Next move the point along the normal to find its closest surface location.

scenes.title: 지형의 높이와 기준선
lines: Keep a horizontal floor model at a fixed height and move a point above and below it. The blue arrow is its upward normal.
The sign of the height difference distinguishes above and below the same reference plane.
Now keep the point and floor unchanged and alter only the viewpoint. The screen bottom is not a fixed world floor. Compare the point and reference plane in the same coordinate frame.
For a horizontal reference, subtract its height from y. A tilted surface instead needs distance along its normal.
Replacing layered floors with one infinite plane loses holes and edges. Surface distance and boundary checks are separate.
Next calculate the closest point on our explicitly defined plane. This does not establish that the earlier game uses the same implementation.

scenes.title: 거리에서 실제로 이동할 점으로
lines: We now know the point-to-plane distance. The next question is where to move the point to reach the nearest surface location.
A slanted route adds sideways travel; the perpendicular route is shortest. The same floor has height2. Keep x and z and change y to2. A unit normal does this for a tilted plane.

scenes.title: 평면 위의 가장 가까운 점
lines: Point four, five, minus three has signed distance three from the y two plane.
Move three units opposite its normal. The closest plane point is four, two, minus three.
With a unit normal, subtract signed distance times that normal from the query.
With an unnormalized normal, multiply it by the residual divided by its squared length, then subtract.
Behind the plane, negative signed distance moves the point toward the normal. One formula handles both sides.
This projection finds the nearest point on an infinite plane. Beyond a triangle or platform edge, the nearest point on that bounded surface needs a separate test.

scenes.title: 표면을 보았으니 법선도 직접 만들 수 있을까요?
lines: So far we chose the normal in advance. Given three vertices, we need to construct an orientation from their coordinates. Use two edges starting at one vertex. This diagram lies in x and y, with z perpendicular to it.

Edges six and four make a rectangle of area twenty-four. Their cross product points perpendicular to both edges; its magnitude is parallelogram area. The triangle has half that area, twelve. Distinguish orientation order from area magnitude.

scenes.title: 세 점으로 법선 만들기
lines: Three noncollinear points determine a plane. Form two edge vectors from the same vertex.
Edges six, zero, zero and zero, four, zero have cross product zero, zero, twenty-four.
Using our right-handed first-edge cross second-edge convention gives unit normal zero, zero, one.
Swapping the edge order reverses the normal. Define winding and front-face conventions together.
Dot any one vertex with the normal to obtain d. All three z coordinates are zero here, so d is zero.
Collinear points yield a zero cross product. Nearly collinear inputs may also be poorly conditioned; check before normalization.

scenes.title: 눈에 보이는 삼각형 표식을 관찰하기
lines: Triangles are constructed in the bridge editor.
Observe three joints and the lines between them. A side-view drawing is not automatically a three-dimensional surface. The same surface can appear flattened from a different camera direction.
Ordering three points around the boundary defines a front-face direction. Reversing that order reverses the chosen normal.
A triangular structure does not reveal the bridge’s entire rendering mesh. Here we choose three points to construct a mathematical triangle.
Move a point within the triangle and observe its proximity to each vertex. The next episode expresses this relative location numerically.
First we will handle more than three ordered vertices, then calculate triangle lengths and area.

scenes.title: 방향이 바뀌어도 경계 순서를 따라갑니다
lines: Now use a five-vertex panel instead of a triangle. Tilting the same panel changes the projected outline; hidden edges are distinguished.
The plane location alone does not define the panel’s edge. Gather its vertices in perimeter order, returning from the last to the first, to find the orientation defined by the boundary.

scenes.title: 세 점에서 여러 꼭짓점의 표면으로
lines: Three points gave a triangle orientation. For a larger boundary with many vertices, an arbitrary selection of three might be almost collinear.

The next method accumulates contributions from neighboring boundary points, returning from the last to the first. Newell names this ordered-boundary method; it is not a method for randomly shuffled points.

scenes.title: 여러 꼭짓점에는 순서가 필요합니다
lines: Choosing any three polygon vertices can be unstable when they are nearly collinear or lie at a concave corner.
Newell method accumulates contributions from adjacent vertices in boundary order, including the closing edge.
Its z component sums each neighboring x difference times their y sum. Cycle the coordinates for the other components.
Reversing boundary order reverses the normal. Arbitrarily shuffled points are not valid ordered input.
Once the normal is chosen, average its dot products with vertices to obtain d, equivalently dot the mean point with the normal.
The source calls this best fit, but it is not generally the least-squares plane of an unordered point cloud. Validate point count and degeneracy separately.

scenes.title: 표면까지 왔지만 끝을 넘었을 수 있습니다
lines: This episode defined surface orientation, point-to-plane distance and the closest plane point. We separated residual from distance and checked vertex order.
A plane has no edge. A projected point can lie on the plane beyond the actual platform. Next, carry that point into a finite triangle and describe its location with three numbers.
